experiment_design.technical_details: This experiment tests the hypothesis that non-commutative algebraic structures (quantum groups) provide a more efficient mathematical substrate for modeling neural synchronization than classical commutative manifolds. We will implement a Quantum Group Neural Network (QGNN) layer where weight updates and state transitions follow the composition laws of quantum group coordinates as defined in EV-Q123-a36b3b0492e4d6391492f5e1. Specifically, the layer will enforce non-trivial commutation relations [x_i, x_j] != 0, parameterized by a deformation parameter alpha. The model will be trained to predict phase-locking values (PLV) from raw EEG/MEG time-series data. The core mechanism relies on the isomorphism between the categorical synchronicity structures in quantum games (EV-Q123-6db737cdd9c8f028232e259e) and neural coupling metrics. We will compare this against classical RNNs and LSTMs with equivalent parameter counts.
